security_audit.summary: Most static command execution alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, inline file paths, and JavaScript RegExp.exec. The confirmed issues are low-severity third-party network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts. I found no evidence of credential access, data exfiltration, destructive commands, or prompt injection attempts.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js with the artifact template or pin the CDN script with integrity metadata and a documented version review process.
Use local font files or system font fallbacks when privacy or offline use matters, and disclose any external font requests.

content.value_statement: Generative art requests often need structure, reproducibility, and usable controls. This skill turns a creative idea into a p5.js artwork with seeded variation and an interactive viewer.
actual_capabilities: Creates a written algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Guides p5.js sketches that use seeded random and noise values.
Builds a single self-contained HTML artifact with inline controls.
Uses a viewer template with seed navigation, parameter sliders, and actions.
Supports downloadable PNG output through the viewer template.
Encourages original generative systems instead of copying artist styles.
limitations: Generated artifacts may load p5.js and fonts from external CDNs.
The skill provides guidance and templates, not a finished art engine.
Complex sketches can still need manual performance tuning.
It is focused on browser-based p5.js, not native rendering pipelines.

use_cases.title: Explore a Visual Concept
use_cases.description: Turn a mood, theme, or reference into a reproducible generative artwork with adjustable parameters.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interactive Artifacts
use_cases.description: Create a browser-ready p5.js viewer for experiments, demos, and client reviews.

use_cases.title: Teach Generative Systems
use_cases.description: Show how philosophy, seeded randomness, and parameter controls shape algorithmic art.

prompt_templates.title: Start From a Mood
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a first artwork.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art piece about quiet ocean movement. Include the philosophy and a self-contained p5.js viewer.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Tunable System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create generative art from the idea of urban growth. Add controls for density, speed, variation, and color balance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Seeded Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an algorithmic art system with seed navigation. Highlight three seeds that show distinct but related visual outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for iteration and critique.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine this generative art concept for stronger composition, better performance, and clearer parameter controls. Keep the viewer template structure.

output_examples.input: Create a generative artwork inspired by magnetic fields.
output_examples.output: A short philosophy about invisible forces, plus an interactive p5.js viewer with seed controls and field strength sliders.

output_examples.input: Make an artwork about city lights after rain.
output_examples.output: A browser-ready artifact with layered particle reflections, adjustable density, palette controls, and reproducible seed navigation.

output_examples.input: Create 100 variations of a recursive botanical system.
output_examples.output: A single viewer that supports seed exploration, reset actions, and downloadable PNG captures for selected variations.

best_practices: Start with the algorithmic philosophy, then choose code structures that express it clearly.
Keep seed behavior deterministic so users can revisit and share specific outputs.
Tune parameter ranges for useful exploration instead of exposing every internal variable.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a living artist style or reproduce copyrighted artwork.
Do not replace the viewer template with unrelated layout or branding.
Do not rely on random noise alone without composition, constraints, or intent.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a written generative art concept and a self-contained p5.js HTML viewer.

faq.question: Can outputs be reproduced?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions require seeded randomness so the same seed produces the same result.

faq.question: Does it need a server?
faq.answer: No. The generated HTML is intended to open directly in a browser or Claude artifact.

faq.question: Can users adjust the artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes seed controls, parameter controls, reset, regenerate, and PNG download actions.

faq.question: Does it generate raster images directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides creation of interactive browser artifacts that can export PNG captures.

faq.question: Are there external dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. The provided template loads p5.js and Google Fonts from public CDNs unless modified.
